Śuka Sūtra (170), Chapter on Fundamental Analysis, Śuka Sūtra, the Ninth, Fourth Analysis.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

Then, when the night had passed and it was dawn, the World-Honored One dressed, took his bowl, and entered Śrāvastī for alms. While on his almsround, he went to the house of the young brahmin Māṭhara, the son of Tuṇḍila, who was a parrot.
At that time, the young brahmin student Śuka Māṇava, son of Todeyya, had gone out on some business and was not at home.
At that moment, a white dog belonging to the household of Śuka Māṇava, son of Todeyya, was eating from a golden plate upon a large couch.
Thereupon, the white dog saw the Buddha approaching from afar, and having seen him, it began to bark.
The World-Honored One said to the white dog:
"You should not do this; you have gone from growling to barking."
Having heard this, the white dog became extremely enraged; it descended from its bed and went to the side of a pile of wood, lying there in sorrowful dejection.

Later, when the parrot-son Māṇava Dōṭiputta returned home, he saw his white dog extremely enraged, having descended from its bed and gone to the side of the pile of wood, lying there in sorrowful dejection. He asked the family members:
"Who has provoked my dog, causing it to become so extremely enraged that it descended from its bed and went to the side of the pile of wood to lie there in sorrowful dejection?"
The family members replied,
"We have not at all provoked or disturbed the white dog to cause it such great anger that it jumped down from its bed and lies dejected and sorrowful by the side of the woodpile."
"Mañjuśrī!
You should know that today the śramaṇa Gautama came here to beg for alms; when the white dog saw him, it immediately chased after him and barked at him.
The śramaṇa Gautama said to the white dog:"
"You should not do such a thing as to go from growling to barking.
Because of this, Māṇava, the white dog became extremely enraged;
he descended from his bed, went to the side of a wooden pile, and lay down there, dejected and sorrowful.

Having heard this, the young brahmin student Māṇava Śuka Todeyyaputta became greatly incensed; he sought to misrepresent the Blessed One, to slander the Blessed One, and to bring about the Blessed One’s downfall.
Having thus falsely slandered the śramaṇa Gautama, he departed from Śrāvastī and proceeded to the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by a vast assembly before and behind as he preached the Dharma. Seeing the young brahmin Māṭhara, the son of Tuṇḍila, approaching from afar, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"Do you see the young brahmin Māṭhara, the son of Tuṇḍila, coming?"
He replied, “I see them.
The World-Honored One said:
“Māṇava Śuka, son of Todeyya, having now passed away, will surely be reborn in hell in the time it takes to bend and stretch one’s arm. Why is that?
Because he harbored extreme hatred toward me.”
"If there are sentient beings who, because of a mind of hatred, at the breaking up of the body after death, will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell.
Thereupon, the young brahmin Māṇava Śuka Todeyyaputta went to where the Buddha was and said to the World-Honored One:
"Sramaṇa Gautama!"
"Have you now come to my house to beg for alms?
The World-Honored One replied,
"I have now gone to your house to beg for alms."
“Gautama! What did you say to my white dog that caused it to become so greatly enraged that it descended from its bed and lies down by the side of the woodpile, sorrowful and dejected?”
The Blessed One replied:

"This morning, having dressed and taken my bowl, I entered Śrāvastī for alms. As I proceeded from house to house, I went to your home to beg for food; there, a white dog saw me coming from afar, and upon seeing me, it barked."
I said to the white dog, "You should not act thus, from growling to barking.
Because of this, the white dog became extremely enraged; it descended from its bed and went to the side of a heap of wood, lying there dejected and sorrowful.
The parrot-monk (Śuka-māṇava) asked the Blessed One:
"In a previous life, what was this white dog to me?
The Blessed One replied:
"Stop! Stop, Māṇava!"
“Be careful not to question me; once you have heard this, you will certainly not be pleased.
The parrot youth then asked the Blessed One a second and a third time:
“In a previous life, what was the white dog to me?”
The World-Honored One also repeated his words two or three times, saying:
"Stop! Stop!"
"Mañjuśrī! Be careful not to question me; having heard this, you must certainly not be displeased.
The World-Honored One further addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
“Māṇava, since you have questioned me repeatedly and will not desist,
you should know that this white dog was your father in a previous life, named Dottiya.”
Upon hearing these words, the parrot-monk became even more intensely enraged; he sought to misrepresent the Blessed One, to slander the Blessed One, and to bring about the Blessed One’s downfall.
Thus falsely accusing and slandering the śramaṇa Gautama, he said to the World-Honored One:
"My father, Duti, practiced great generosity and performed grand sacrificial rites; when his body perished and his life ended, he was reborn directly in the Brahma Heaven."
"For what cause and for what reason has he been born among these lowly dogs?
The World-Honored One replied,
"Because of this overweening pride (adhimāna), your father Duti was born among these lowly dogs."
“Brahmin, you are full of overweening pride; after death you will be reborn in six places:
as a rooster, a dog, a pig, a jackal, a donkey, and fifthly, in the hells.
“O Śuka Māṇava! [he said.]
"If you do not believe what I have said, you may return home and say to the white dog:
'If you were my father in a previous life, O white dog, you should return and sit upon the great couch.'"
"O Māṇava! The white dog will surely climb back onto the bed.
If, in a previous life, he was my father, the white dog shall eat from the golden platter."
"O Māṇava! The white dog will surely return to eat from the golden platter.
'If in a previous life you were my father, show me the places where I have buried gold, silver, crystal, and precious treasures—those which I do not know.'"
"O Māṇava! That white dog will surely show you the previously hidden places where gold, silver, crystal, and precious treasures were stored—places that you do not know."

Thereupon, the young brahmin Śuka, having heard what the Buddha had said, received and recited it well; he circumambulated the World-Honored One and returned to his home, where he spoke to the white dog, saying:
"If you were my father in a previous life, then, white dog, you should return and lie upon the great bed."
The white dog immediately returned to the large bed.
[The prince said: "If in a previous life you were my father, then let the white dog return to eat from the golden platter.
The white dog immediately returned to the golden platter and ate.
"If he were my father in a previous life, he should show me the locations where my father originally buried his stores of gold, silver, crystal, and precious gems—places of which I am unaware."

The white dog immediately descended from the bed and went to the place where it had lived in its previous life; there, with its mouth and paws, it dug up the four legs of the bed, and the parrot-monk (Śuka-māṇava) thus obtained a great quantity of treasures from that spot.

Then, having obtained the treasures, the parrot-monk Dutiya was filled with great joy. He knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Jeta Grove Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, and three times raised his voice in praise of the World-Honored One:
“The words spoken by the śramaṇa Gautama are not in vain; the words spoken by the śramaṇa Gautama are the ultimate truth; the words spoken by the śramaṇa Gautama are according to reality.”
Having praised him thus a second and a third time, he departed from Śrāvastī and proceeded to the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

At that time, the World-honored One was surrounded by an immeasurable great assembly who were listening to his teaching of the Dharma. Seeing the young brahmin Śuka approaching from afar, the World-honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“Do you see the young brahmin Śuka coming?”
He replied, “I have seen them.
The World-Honored One said:
"If Śuka Māṇava were to pass away this very moment, as quickly as one might bend or stretch an arm, he would surely go to a good destination. Why is that?
Because he possesses an exceedingly virtuous mind toward me."
"If there are sentient beings who, because of a virtuous mind, at the breaking up of the body after death, will certainly go to a good destination and be reborn among the devas.
At that time, the parrot youth Māṇava went to where the Buddha was, exchanged greetings with him, and sat down to one side. The World-Honored One said to him:
"How is it, Māṇava?"
“Is it as I have described regarding the white dog,
or is it not so? Śuka Māṇava replied:
"Gautama! It is truly as you have said. Gautama!"
"I wish further to ask a question; if you grant me leave, I shall venture to state it.
The World-Honored One replied, "Ask whatever you wish."

“Gautama! By what cause and by what condition do those beings, though all receiving a human body, differ in status—some being superior and others inferior, some excellent and others not? Why is this so?”

"Gautama! I see some who are short-lived and some who are long-lived; I see some who are afflicted by much illness and some who have little illness; I see some who are unattractive and some who are handsome; I see some who lack majesty and some who possess majesty; I see some from low-born families and some from noble families; I see some who possess no wealth and some who possess wealth; I see some with evil wisdom and some with virtuous wisdom."
The Blessed One replied:

"Those sentient beings, by reason of their own karma, receive retribution according to that karma; conditioned by karma, dependent on karma, and having karma as their basis, sentient beings dwell in high or low, excellent or inferior states according to their respective actions."
The young brahmin Śuka addressed the Blessed One, saying:

"The teaching spoken by the śramaṇa Gautama is extremely brief and not extensively analyzed; I am unable to understand it. I pray that the śramaṇa Gautama will explain it to me in detail, so that I may come to know its meaning."
The World-Honored One said:
"Māṇava! Listen attentively and reflect upon it well; I shall explain it to you in detail."
The parrot youth replied:
"Indeed, I shall receive your instruction with attentive ears."
The Buddha said:
"Māṇava! For what cause and for what reason do men and women have such extremely short lifespans?"

If there are men or women who kill living beings, being cruel and wicked, extremely evil and bloodthirsty, harboring harmful intentions and dwelling upon evil, lacking any heart of compassion toward sentient beings—even down to the smallest insects—they will undergo this karma. Having fully committed these deeds, when their bodies perish at the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. Should they later be reborn among humans, their lifespan will be exceedingly short.
Why is that? This path leads to a short life;
it is the way of men and women who are murderous, cruel, and extremely evil blood-drinkers. O Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women attain an extremely long lifespan?

If there are men or women who abstain from killing and sever the act of killing, laying aside the sword and staff, possessing a sense of shame and dread of blame, and with a heart of loving-kindness and compassion, benefiting all beings down to the smallest insects—having performed and fulfilled this karma, when their bodies perish at the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a happy destination and be born among the devas; should they later be born in the human world, their lifespan will be exceedingly long.
Why is that? This path leads to long life, namely, for men and women who abstain from killing and have severed the practice of killing. Māṇava!
"You should know that such karma has such a retribution. "Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women frequently suffer from illness?"

If there are men or women who harass living beings—whether with their hands or fists, or with wood, stones, or knives and staves—and having performed such actions to completion, when their body breaks up at the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell; if they later take birth among humans, they will suffer from many diseases.
Why is that? This path brings about much illness, namely, the harassment of living beings by men and women. O Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women have no illness?

If there are men or women who do not harass living beings—neither with their hands or fists, nor with wood or stones, nor with swords or staves—they perform this action fully and completely; then, at the breaking up of the body after death, they will surely ascend to a happy destination and be born among the devas, and when they return to birth as humans, they will be free from disease.
Why is this so? Because this path brings freedom from illness; that is to say, whether man or woman, one does not harass or disturb living beings. Māṇava!
"You should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what condition are men and women of unattractive appearance?"

If there are men or women who are irritable and prone to much vexation, they become greatly enraged upon hearing even a little; they give rise to hatred, envy, and sorrow, and extensively produce contention and anger. Having performed and completed such karma, when their body breaks up at the end of life, they will inevitably go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they later take birth among humans, their physical form will not be upright or handsome.
Why is that? Because those who take form through this path are not handsome; that is to say, men and women are quick-tempered and full of vexation, Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
By what cause and by what condition do men and women possess upright and handsome physical forms?

If there are men or women who are not impetuous and have little affliction, they will not become greatly enraged upon hearing soft, harsh, or forceful words; they will not give rise to hatred, envy, or sorrow, nor will they extensively produce contention or anger. Having performed and completed this karma, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the devas; when they later return to birth in the human world, their physical form will be upright and handsome.
Why is that? Because this path leads to receiving a physical form that is upright and handsome— meaning one is neither quick-tempered nor prone to much affliction,
whether man or woman, Māṇava!
"You should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women lack majesty and virtue?"

If there are men or women who harbor jealousy within their hearts, and upon seeing others receive offerings and respect, they give rise to envy; or if they see that others possess certain things and desire for themselves to obtain them—having performed such actions and brought them to completion, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they will inevitably go to an evil destination and be born in hell. Should they later be reborn among humans, they will lack majesty and virtue.
Why is that? This path receives no majesty because men and women harbor jealousy within their hearts. O Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
By what cause and by what condition do men and women possess great majestic power?

If there are men or women who do not harbor jealousy—such that when they see others receiving offerings and respect, they do not give rise to envy; or when they see others possess wealth, they do not wish for themselves to obtain it—they perform this karma to its full completion. When their body breaks up and their life ends, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the devas; when they later return to birth in the human world, they will possess great majesty and virtue.
Why is that? Because this path brings about majesty and virtue, such that men and women do not harbor jealousy. Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. "Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason are men and women born into low-born families?"

If there are men or women who are arrogant and conceited, who do not show respect to those worthy of respect, do not honor those worthy of honor, do not value those worthy of value, do not serve those worthy of service, do not make offerings to those worthy of offerings, do not offer the Way to those worthy of it, do not offer a seat to those worthy of one, and do not join their palms in salutation and inquiry to those worthy of such greeting—having performed these actions fully and having received the karmic fruit thereof, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell; if they later return to birth among humans, they will be born into a low and base lineage.
Why is that? This path leads to birth in a lowly family, namely among men and women who are arrogant and excessively conceited. O Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason are men and women born into noble families?

If there are men or women who are not arrogant or conceited, and who respect those worthy of respect, honor those worthy of honor, esteem those worthy of esteem, serve those worthy of service, make offerings to those worthy of offerings, offer a seat to those worthy of a seat, and join their palms in salutation and inquiry to those worthy of such salutation and inquiry—having performed these actions fully and completed them, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they will surely ascend to a happy destination and be reborn among the devas; and when they return to birth in the human world, they will be born into a noble and distinguished clan.
Why is that? This path leads to rebirth in a noble and distinguished clan, meaning that whether man or woman, one is neither conceited nor arrogant. O Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. "Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women lack wealth?"

If there are men or women who do not act as donors and do not practice giving—failing to bestow upon śramaṇas, brahmins, the poor, the solitary, and beggars from afar food and drink, clothing and bedding, flower garlands, scented ointments, dwellings, couches, bright lamps, and attendants—they, having performed and completed this karma, will at the breaking up of the body after death, inevitably go to an evil destination and be born in hell; and when they later take birth among humans, they will possess no wealth or goods.
Why is that? This path receives no material wealth; that is to say, men and women do not act as donors and do not practice giving. Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women possess great wealth?

If there are men or women who act as donors and practice giving, bestowing upon śramaṇas, brahmins, the poor, the solitary, and beggars from afar food and drink, clothing and bedding, flower garlands, fragrant ointments, dwellings, couches, bright lamps, and attendants—if they receive this karma and bring it to completion, then at the breaking up of the body after death, they will certainly ascend to a happy destination and be born among the devas; when they later return to birth in the human world, they will possess abundant wealth and property.
Why is that? Because this path receives many material goods; that is to say, men and women act as donors and practice giving, O Māṇava!
"You should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
For what cause and for what reason do men and women possess evil wisdom?"

If there are men or women who do not frequently go to visit them to inquire about matters, and if there are sramanas or brahmins of renown and virtue whom they do not visit from time to time to ask about the meaning [of the Dharma], saying:
"Venerable sirs!..."
What is wholesome and what is unwholesome?
What is a transgression and what is not a transgression?
What is sublime and what is not sublime?
What is white, and what is black?
From what do the white and black arise?
In what sense is there retribution in the present life, and in what sense is there retribution in future lives?

"Even if one does not act upon it when questioned, having fully completed that karma and received its fruit, at the breaking up of the body after death, one will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell; and when reborn among humans, one will possess evil wisdom."
Why is that? Because this path receives unwholesome wisdom; that is to say, men and women do not frequently go to him to inquire about matters. Māṇava!
One should know that such karma has such a retribution. Māṇava!
By what cause and by what condition do men and women possess wholesome wisdom?

If there are men or women who frequently go to those [teachers] to inquire about matters, and if there are sramanas or brahmins of renown and virtue whom they frequently visit at appropriate times to ask about the meaning [of the teachings]:
"Venerable sirs!..."
What is wholesome and what is unwholesome?
What is an offense and what is not an offense?
What is sublime and what is not sublime?
What is white and what is black?
From what do the white and black arise?
In what sense is there retribution in the present life, and in what sense is there retribution in future lives?

Having been thus questioned, he was able to practice; having undertaken this karma and brought it to completion, at the breaking up of the body after death, he will certainly ascend to a happy destination and be reborn among the devas. When he returns to birth in the human world, he will possess wholesome wisdom.
Why is that? Because this path receives wholesome wisdom;
that is to say, men and women who are able to go repeatedly to him to inquire about matters. Māṇava!
One should know that this karma has such a retribution. "Māṇava!

One should know that by performing karma associated with a short lifespan, one will certainly obtain a short lifespan; by performing karma associated with a long lifespan, one will certainly [obtain a long lifespan]."
One attains long life; by performing karma associated with many diseases, one will certainly experience many diseases;
by performing karma associated with few diseases, one will certainly experience few diseases; by performing karma associated with ugliness, one will certainly attain ugliness;
by performing karma associated with physical excellence, one will certainly attain physical excellence; and by performing karma associated with a lack of majesty...
Karma inevitably results in a lack of majesty; karma corresponding to majesty results in majesty;
karma corresponding to a lowly lineage results in a lowly lineage; karma corresponding to a noble lineage results in a noble lineage;
karma corresponding to a lack of wealth results in a lack of wealth; and karma corresponding to great wealth results in great wealth.
If one performs an action associated with material things, one will certainly obtain abundant wealth; if one performs an evil action associated with wisdom, one will certainly obtain evil wisdom;
and if one performs a virtuous action associated with wisdom, one will certainly obtain virtuous wisdom.

"O Māṇava! This is what I have previously taught: Sentient beings, due to their own performed karma, receive retribution because of that karma; conditioned by karma and dependent upon karma, beings abide in high or low, superior or inferior states according to their karma."
The young brahmin Māṇava Śuka Todeyyaputta said:
“World-Honored One,
I have understood.”
"Sugata! I have understood.
World-Honored One!"

I now take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus; I pray only that the World-Honored One accept me as a lay follower (upāsaka). From this day forth, until the end of my life, I take refuge for as long as I live.
World-Honored One!

From this day forward, when you enter the home of Cunda, may it be as if you were entering the homes of the lay followers (upāsakas) here in Śrāvastī, so that Cunda’s family may long obtain benefit and virtue, and attain abundance, peace, and happiness.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
Having heard what the Buddha had said, the Māṇava Śuka Todeyyaputta and the vast assembly rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

The ninth *Śuka Sūtra* ends here, totaling three thousand four hundred and sixty-five characters. 171. *Mahākammavibhaṅga Sūtra* (171), Middle Discourses, Fundamental Analysis Section, *Mahākammavibhaṅga Sūtra*, the tenth discourse, the fourth recitation section. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was traveling through Rājagṛha and staying at the Bamboo Grove, the Kalandaka Garden.
At that time, the Venerable Samiddhi was also traveling through Rājagṛha and dwelling in a secluded meditation hut.
Then, later in the day, the wanderer Pūraṇa Kāśyapa was wandering about when he went to where the Venerable Samitiya was; having exchanged greetings with him, he sat down to one side.
“Venerable Sammitta!
I wish to ask you something; will you allow me to ask?
The Venerable Sammitta replied:
“Venerable Pūraṇa-putra!
Ask whatever you wish to ask; having heard it, I shall reflect upon it.
Then the heterodox Pūraṇa-putra asked:
“O Bhadanta Samiti!

I have heard this directly from the Śramaṇa Gautama and received it directly from the Śramaṇa Gautama: ‘Bodily and vocal actions are false; only mental action is the ultimate truth. There may be a concentration such that when a bhikṣu enters that concentration, he has no perception.’”
The Venerable Samiddhi said:
"Worthy son of Pūraṇa! Do not speak thus;
do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is unwholesome to misrepresent the Blessed One."
The Blessed One does not speak thus, O son of Bhāradvāja. The Blessed One, by means of immeasurable skillful methods, has said:

"If one intentionally performs an action, and that action is completed, I declare that there is no such deed whose retribution will not be experienced—either to be experienced in this very life, or to be experienced in a future life."
"If an action is performed unintentionally and yet has been completed, I do not say that one must necessarily experience its retribution.
The heterodox teacher Pūraṇa Kassapa spoke thus to the Venerable Samiddhi a second and even a third time: "Worthy Samiddhi!"

I have heard this directly from the Śramaṇa Gautama and received it directly from the Śramaṇa Gautama: bodily and verbal actions are false, while only mental action is the ultimate truth; furthermore, there is a meditative concentration such that when a bhikṣu enters that concentration, he has no perception whatsoever.
The Venerable Samiddhi also replied a second and a third time:
"Worthy son of Pūraṇa! Do not speak thus;
do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for to misrepresent the Blessed One is unwholesome."
The Blessed One does not speak thus,
O son of Bhūridatta! By means of immeasurable skillful methods,

the Blessed One has taught that if one intentionally performs an action and it is brought to completion, I declare that there is no such karma that will not bear its fruit— whether it be experienced in this very life or in a future life.
"If one performs an action unintentionally, and it has been completed, I do not say that one will necessarily experience its retribution.
The heterodox teacher Pūraṇa Kāśyapa asked the Venerable Samiddhi:
"If one performs an action intentionally, and it has been completed, what kind of retribution will one receive?"
The Venerable Samiddhi replied:
"Worthy son of Pūraṇa!
If one intentionally performs an action and that action has been completed, one will necessarily experience its suffering."
The wanderer Pūraṇa Kaśyapa again asked the Venerable Samiddhi: "Worthy Samiddhi!
For how long have you been training in this Dharma and Vinaya?"
The Venerable Samiddhi replied: "Worthy Potaliputta!
I have not long studied this Dhamma and Vinaya; it has been only three years since I began."
Thereupon, the wanderer Pūraṇa Kāśyapa thought to himself:
"If even this young bhikṣu can protect his teacher, how much more so those who are long-established, venerable, and highly esteemed?"
Thereupon, having heard what the Venerable Samiddhi had said, the heterodox teacher Pūraṇa Kāśyapa neither approved nor disapproved; he rose from his seat, shook his head, and departed.
At that time, the Venerable Mahācunda was not far from the place where the Venerable Samiddhi was sitting for his midday rest.

Thereupon, the Venerable Mahācunda, having fully recited and properly mastered everything that had been discussed between the Venerable Samiddhi and the heterodox Pūraṇa Kāśyapa, rose from his seat, went to the Venerable Ānanda, exchanged greetings with him, and sat down to one side.
The Venerable Samiddhi related in full to the Venerable Ānanda everything that had been discussed with the heterodox Pūraṇa Kāśyapa.
Having heard this, the Venerable Ānanda said:
"Worthy Cunda!..."
"By means of this discourse, we may go to see the Buddha and present it to the World-Honored One. Worthy Cunda!
Let us now go together to the Buddha and explain this matter in detail to the World-Honored One; perhaps by this means we may hear some further Dharma from the World-Honored One."
Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Mahācunda went together to visit the Buddha.
The Venerable Mahācunda prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and sat down to one side; the Venerable Ānanda prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda said:
"Worthy Mahācunda! You may speak; you may speak."
Thereupon, the Blessed One asked:
"Ānanda, what matter does the bhikkhu Cunda wish to speak about?"
The Venerable Ānanda replied:
“World-Honored One,
I shall now hear it myself.”
Thereupon, the Venerable Mahācunda related to the Buddha everything that had been discussed between the Venerable Samiddhi and the wanderer Potaliputta.
Having heard this, the Blessed One said: "Ānanda!
Behold the foolish and unprincipled bhikṣu Samiti."
"Why is that? The heterodox teacher Pūraṇa Kāśyapa asked an uncertain question, yet the foolish bhikṣu Samiti answered categorically.
Venerable Ānanda said:
“World-Honored One!
If the bhikṣu Samiti were to speak on this matter, saying that all perceptions are suffering, what fault would there be?
The World-Honored One rebuked the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"Look! The bhikṣu Ānanda likewise has no path. Ānanda!"
This foolish man, Samiti, questioned that heterodox teacher Pūraṇa Kāśyapa about all three types of feeling: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Ānanda! If the foolish person Samiti were questioned by the heterodox Pūradāyin, and he answered in this way:
"Venerable Pūradāyin!..."
If one intentionally performs a pleasant action and it is completed, one shall receive the retribution of pleasure;
if one intentionally performs a painful action and it is completed, one shall receive the retribution of pain;
if one intentionally performs a neither-painful-nor-pleasant action and it is completed, one shall receive the retribution of neither-pain-nor-pleasure.

“Ānanda! If the foolish person Samiti were questioned by the heterodox Pūraṇa Kāśyapa and answered in such a manner, the heterodox Pūraṇa Kāśyapa would not even dare to look at the foolish person Samiti, let alone be able to question him on such a matter.”
“Ānanda!
If you were to question the Blessed One regarding the *Mahāsamaya-sūtra*, your mind would become even more serene toward the Tathāgata and you would attain joy.
Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda joined his palms toward the Buddha and said:
“World-Honored One!
Now is precisely the right time. Sugata!”
Now is precisely the right time.
If the World-Honored One were to preach the Mahākarmavibhaṅga-sūtra for the bhikṣus, the bhikṣus, having heard it, would properly receive and uphold it.
The Blessed One said:
“Ānanda! Listen attentively and reflect upon it well; I shall explain it to you in full detail.”
The Venerable Ānanda replied, “So be it.
Then the bhikṣus received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said: “Ānanda!

Suppose there is one who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain and fail to guard himself against these, at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a good destination, among the devas.”

Ānanda! There may be someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; yet, having practiced such abstinence and restraint, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell.

Ānanda! There may be someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain and fail to guard themselves against these, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell.

Ānanda! There may be someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having thus abstained and guarded himself, at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.

“Ānanda! Suppose there is one who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain from these and failing to guard against them, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a good destination, among the devas. What do you think, Ānanda?”
If there are recluses or brahmins who have attained the divine eye and, having perfected the divine eye, see that [reality], and having seen it, they form this thought:
"There is no bodily misconduct, nor is there any retribution for bodily misconduct; there is no verbal or mental misconduct, nor is there any retribution for verbal or mental misconduct."

Why is that? I see that they did not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; yet, despite not abstaining and not guarding themselves against these, at the breaking up of the body after death, they were reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.

If there were others of this kind who did not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—and who neither desisted from nor guarded against these—yet all of them, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, would likewise be reborn in a good destination, among the devas.
"One who views it in this way possesses right view; one whose view differs from this, does their wisdom not tend toward the heterodox?

If they grasp at what is seen and known with all their might, adhering single-mindedly to their own assertions and claiming, 'This alone is the ultimate truth; everything else is false'—[this is the case]."

“Ānanda! Suppose there is one who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having thus abstained and guarded himself, yet at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in an evil destination, in hell. [Why is this?]”
If there are recluses or brahmins who have attained the divine eye and, having perfected the divine eye, see that [rebirth], and having seen it, form this thought:

"There is no bodily wholesome conduct, nor is there any fruit of bodily wholesome conduct; there is no verbal or mental wholesome conduct, nor is there any fruit of verbal or mental wholesome conduct."

Why is that? I have seen those who abstained from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; yet, despite having abandoned and guarded against these, at the breaking up of the body after death, they were reborn in an evil destination, in hell.

If there are others who likewise abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong views—and who thus abstain and guard themselves—all such persons, upon the dissolution of the body after death, will likewise be reborn in an evil destination, in hell.
"One who views it in this way possesses right view; one whose view differs from this, does their wisdom not tend toward the heterodox?
If one grasps at what is seen and known with all one's might, adhering single-mindedly to the claim that 'this alone is the ultimate truth and all else is false,' [one falls into error]."

“Ānanda! Suppose there is one who does not refrain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to refrain from and guard against these, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell.
If there are recluses or brahmins who have attained the divine eye, who have perfected the divine eye and see that [rebirth], and having seen it, they form this thought:
"There are bodily misdeeds, and there is also the retribution for bodily misdeeds; there are verbal and mental misdeeds, and there is also the retribution for verbal and mental misdeeds."

Why is that? I see that they do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain from these and failed to guard themselves, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a miserable destination, in hell.

If there are others of this kind who do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—if they do not abstain from these and do not guard themselves—then all of them, upon the breakup of the body after death, will likewise be reborn in an evil destination, in hell.
"One who views it thus possesses right view; one whose view differs from this, does their wisdom not tend toward the wrong?
If they grasp at what is seen and known with all their might, adhering single-mindedly to their own assertions, saying, 'This alone is the ultimate truth, and all else is false.'"

“Ānanda! Suppose there is one who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having abstained from these and guarded himself, at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.
If there are recluses or brahmins who have attained the divine eye, who have perfected the divine eye and see that [rebirth], and having seen it, they form this thought:
"There is bodily good conduct, and there is the fruit of bodily good conduct; there is verbal and mental good conduct, and there is also the fruit of verbal and mental good conduct."

Why is that? Because I see that those who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—having thus abstained and guarded themselves—upon the breakup of the body after death, are reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.

If there are others who likewise abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—if they abstain from these and guard themselves against them—all such persons, upon the dissolution of the body after death, will also be reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.
"One who sees in this way possesses right view; one whose view differs from this, does their wisdom not tend toward the wrong?

If they grasp at what is seen and known with all their might, adhering single-mindedly to their own assertions and claiming, 'This alone is the ultimate truth, and all else is false'—[is this not a sign of delusion]?"
"Ānanda! Suppose among them there is a certain śramaṇa or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, perfected the divine eye, and speaks thus:
'There is no bodily misconduct, nor is there retribution for bodily misconduct; there is no verbal or mental misconduct, nor is there retribution for verbal or mental misconduct.'"
As for those who say this, I do not accept their view. If they were to say:

"I see that one who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong views—having failed to abstain from and guard against these—upon the breakup of the body after death, is reborn in a good destination, among the devas."
"I have heard him say this: 'If there are others like these who do not abstain from killing,

taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on, up to wrong view— if they do not abstain from these and do not guard themselves, yet at the breaking up of the body after death, they too are reborn in a good destination, among the devas.'"
As for those who say this, I do not approve of them. If they were to say:
"One who holds such a view possesses right view; one whose view differs from this has an intellect that tends toward the wrong," [I would not approve].
As for those who say this, I do not grant them my approval.

If they grasp at what they have seen and known with all their might, adhering single-mindedly to their own assertions and claiming, "This alone is the ultimate truth; everything else is false," I do not grant them my approval.
Why is this so? Ānanda!
The Tathāgata knows that person to be different.
“Ānanda! Suppose among them there is a certain śramaṇa or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, perfected the divine eye, and speaks thus:

‘There is no bodily wholesome conduct, nor is there any result of bodily wholesome conduct; there is no verbal or mental wholesome conduct, nor is there any result of verbal or mental wholesome conduct.’”
I do not accept that. If one were to say:

"I see that person who has abstained from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having thus abstained and guarded himself, at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a miserable destination, in hell."
"I have heard this from him.
If it were said:

'If there are others who, in a similar manner, abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even up to wrong view—and who thus abstain and guard themselves—all such persons, upon the breakup of the body after death, will likewise be reborn in an evil destination, in hell.'"
As for those who say this, I do not approve of them. If they were to say:
"One who holds such a view possesses right view; one whose view differs from this has an intellect that inclines toward the wrong," [I would not approve].
As for those who say this, I do not grant them my approval.

If they grasp at what they have seen and known with all their might, and speak with one-sided attachment, claiming, "This alone is the ultimate truth; all else is false," I do not grant them my approval.
Why is this so? Ānanda!
The Tathāgata knows that person to be different.
“Ānanda! Suppose among them there is a certain ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, perfected the divine eye, and declares:
‘There is bodily misconduct, and there is the retribution for bodily misconduct; there is verbal and mental misconduct, and there is also the retribution for verbal and mental misconduct.’”
"I accept that statement.
If one were to say:

'I see that person who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain from these and failing to guard against them, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell.'"
I grant that to him. If one were to say:

"If there are others who likewise do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—if they do not abstain from these and do not guard themselves, then all such persons, upon the breakup of the body after death, will also be reborn in an evil destination, in hell. I grant that to him as well.
As for those who say this, I do not approve of them. If they were to say:
"One who holds such a view possesses right view; one whose view differs from this has an intellect that inclines toward what is wrong," [I would not approve].
As for such a person, I do not approve of them.
If they grasp at what they have seen and known with all their might, adhering to it one-sidedly and declaring, "This alone is the ultimate truth; everything else is false," I do not approve of them.
Why is this? Ānanda! The Tathāgata knows that person to be different.
“Ānanda! Suppose among them there is a certain śramaṇa or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, perfected the divine eye, and speaks thus:
‘There is bodily good conduct, and there is the fruit of bodily good conduct; there is verbal and mental good conduct, and there is also the fruit of verbal and mental good conduct.’”
As for those who say, "I see that one who abstains from killing, taking what is not given,

sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view— having abandoned these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body after death, is reborn in a happy destination, among the devas"— I grant them this.
As for those who say this, I grant them my approval. If they were to say:

"If there are others such as these who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even up to wrong view—if all such persons, upon the breakup of the body after death, are likewise reborn in a good destination, among the devas," [I would grant them my approval].
As for those who say this, I do not approve of them. If they speak thus:
"One who holds such a view possesses right view; one whose view differs from this has an intellect that inclines toward the wrong."
As for such a person, I do not accept them.

If they grasp at what they have seen and known with all their might, adhering one-sidedly to their own assertions and claiming, "This alone is the ultimate truth; everything else is false," I do not accept them.
Why is this so? Ānanda!
The Tathāgata knows that person to be different.

“Ānanda! Suppose there is one who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view; having failed to abstain and fail to guard himself, yet at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a good destination, among the devas—if he had previously performed unwholesome kamma that has reached completion, it is because of that failure to abstain and failure to guard that he experiences the result in this present life and is subsequently reborn there. Or perhaps it is due to a result of subsequent kamma that he is reborn in a good destination, among the devas, at the breaking up of the body after death, rather than by this specific cause or condition.”

Alternatively, there may be those who have performed wholesome karmas in the past and have brought them to completion; because they have abandoned [unwholesome states] and maintained [the wholesome], the retribution for their wholesome state has not yet been fully exhausted. Due to these causes and conditions, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a good destination, among the devas.

Alternatively, at the time of death, one may give rise to a wholesome mind; when the mental factors associated with right view are present, by reason of this and conditioned by this, upon the breakup of the body after death, one is reborn in a good destination, among the devas.
"Ānanda! The Tathāgata knows that such a person is indeed like this. Ānanda!"

If there is one who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view, and having thus abstained and guarded themselves, at the breaking up of the body after death, is born in an evil destination, in hell—should they have previously performed wholesome kamma that has been completed, it is because of that abstention and guarding that they experience the result in the present life and are subsequently born there.

Or again, due to a result to be experienced in a subsequent life, he—by reason of neither that cause nor that condition—upon the breakup of the body after death, is reborn in an evil destination, in hell.

Furthermore, if one has previously committed unwholesome karma that has been completed, because one does not distance oneself from it nor guard against it, the retribution of hell that ought to be experienced has not yet been exhausted; due to these causes and conditions, at the breaking up of the body after death, one is born in an evil destination, in the hells.

Or again, at the time of death, one may give rise to an unwholesome state of mind, wherein the mental factors are associated with wrong view; by this cause and by this condition, upon the breakup of the body after death, one is reborn in an evil destination, in the hells.
"Ānanda! The Tathāgata knows that such a person is indeed like this. Ānanda!"

If there is one who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view—and having failed to abstain and guard against these—then upon the breakup of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell; it is because of this and on account of this that, upon the breakup of the body after death, they are reborn in an evil destination, in hell.

Furthermore, if one has previously committed unwholesome karma that has been completed, and because one does not abandon or guard against it, the retribution of the hells that ought to be experienced has not yet been exhausted; due to these causes and conditions, at the breaking up of the body after death, one is reborn in an evil destination, in the hells.

Or again, at the time of death, one may give rise to an unwholesome mind, wherein the mental factors are associated with wrong view; by reason of this and through this condition, upon the breakup of the body after death, one is reborn in an evil destination, in the hells.
"Ānanda! The Tathāgata knows that such a person is indeed like this. Ānanda!"

If there is one who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and even wrong view, and having thus abstained and guarded themselves, at the breaking up of the body after death, is reborn in a happy destination, among the devas—it is because of this, on account of this, that at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.

Furthermore, there are those who have performed wholesome karmas in the past and have brought them to completion; because they have abandoned [unwholesome states] and maintained [their vows], the retribution that was to be experienced has not yet been exhausted. On account of this and by reason of this, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.

Alternatively, at the time of death, one may give rise to a wholesome mind; with mental factors associated with right view, by reason of this and through this condition, upon the breakup of the body after death, one is reborn in a happy destination, among the devas.
"Ānanda! The Tathāgata knows that such a person is indeed like this.

Furthermore, there are four kinds of persons: some who do not exist yet appear to exist; some who appear to exist yet do not exist; some who do not exist and appear not to exist; and some who exist and appear to exist."

Ānanda! It is just as with four kinds of mangoes: one that is unripe but appears ripe; one that is ripe but appears unripe; one that is unripe and appears unripe; and one that is ripe and appears ripe.

Thus it is, Ānanda! Regarding these four types of people compared to mangoes: there is one who has nothing but appears to have something; one who has something but appears to have nothing; one who has nothing and appears to have nothing; and one who has something and appears to have something.
Thus the Buddha spoke.
Having heard what the Buddha had said, the Venerable Ānanda and the monks rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
